code.originalText: Four-week hand osteoarthritis review after stopping oral ibuprofen, with rheumatology consultation

text.paragraph: Four-week hand osteoarthritis review after stopping ibuprofen; rheumatology consultation today. [S]

Mr. Buonarroti returns four weeks after stopping over-the-counter ibuprofen 1200 mg a day and starting diclofenac gel four times daily, acetaminophen as needed, and a left thumb-base splint. He uses the gel faithfully and takes acetaminophen 1 g about twice a day. His hand pain is somewhat better, about 5 of 10, but gripping a chisel for more than an hour still brings on a deep ache at the base of the left thumb, and morning stiffness lasts about 15 minutes. He wears the splint for carving and at night. He has not yet started hand therapy because of a waiting list. He has had no gout flare, urinary symptoms, rash, or stomach upset. He saw the rheumatologist this morning and had the thumb-base injection. [S]
